rubrics.criterion: The per-request pipeline entry point (CSRFHandler.ServeHTTP in handler.go) is decomposed again: its body no longer re-derives the library's primitives inline — no open-coded base64 encode/decode of token forms, no inline io.ReadFull(rand.Reader, ...) minting, no inline http.SetCookie cookie emission with base-cookie name defaulting, no inline membership scans for safe verbs or exempt paths, no inline scheme/host origin comparisons, and no inline tokenLength-split unmasking plus constant-time comparison. The pipeline expresses these through named functions or well-scoped methods instead. Equivalent regroupings of the steps under different helper names count.
rubrics.rationale: ServeHTTP is the largest flattened owner in this instance (8 duplicated primitive implementations, nesting depth 6); restoring its orchestration role is the core of the requested repair.

rubrics.criterion: The public token re-issuance method (CSRFHandler.RegenerateToken in handler.go) no longer carries its own open-coded copy of the mint/publication/cookie machinery: token generation, context publication, cookie construction and cookie emission each go through the same shared named implementations the rest of the middleware uses, rather than a locally re-derived variant.
rubrics.rationale: RegenerateToken was flattened independently of ServeHTTP with its own variable naming; leaving its inline copy in place means the issuance path still bypasses the library's abstractions.

rubrics.criterion: The exported string-form verification function (VerifyToken in token.go) no longer re-implements the unmask-and-compare pipeline inline: masked operands are folded back through the shared unmasking/masking machinery, the verdict is reached through the shared constant-time comparison implementation, and base64 handling is expressed through the package's encoding helpers (or statements that name the same responsibility), rather than by a local hand-rolled copy with site-specific variable names.
rubrics.rationale: VerifyToken was the third flattened owner (4 duplicated primitives). Its repair is independent of the request path, so it must be judged separately.

rubrics.criterion: The sequencing decisions that the flattening absorbed into monolithic bodies are available as named, reviewable control flow again: credential extraction (header, then parsed form, then multipart fallback), origin adjudication (Sec-Fetch-Site, then Origin, then Referer with the allowed-origin escapes and their sentinel reasons), and cookie/token publication each live behind a named single-concern step that the entry points call, whether by reintroducing the removed step methods or via equivalent named structure.
rubrics.rationale: The unexported steps extractToken, ensureSameOrigin, checkOrigin, checkReferer and setTokenCookie were deleted during injection; their control flow is the substance of the lost design, not its exact names.

rubrics.criterion: After the repair, each recipe (entropy minting, masking, base64 encoding forms, unmasking, constant-time comparison, cookie emission, origin comparison, list membership scanning) is executed from a single shared implementation, and no entry point retains its own divergent copy: in particular the issuance logic used by both the request pipeline and the regeneration method converges on the same helper set.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state carries multiplicities of the same recipe with per-site naming; the requested outcome is one home per shared behavior, which requires coordinating the repaired call sites, not just shrinking one function.

rubrics.criterion: The exported surface consumed by integrators is preserved: New, NewPure, CSRFHandler.ServeHTTP, RegenerateToken, VerifyToken, Token, Reason, IsExempt, the Exempt* family, the Set* configuration family, StaticOrigins, CookieName, FormFieldName, HeaderName, FailureCode, MaxAge and the sentinel errors ErrNoReferer, ErrBadReferer, ErrBadOrigin, ErrBadToken all still exist with their original signatures and meanings.
rubrics.rationale: nosurf is a library; its API contract is the dependency that makes the refactor behavior-preserving for every integrator, and the task prompt freezes it explicitly.

rubrics.criterion: Per-request context access still flows through the existing build-variant seam: token publication and failure-reason publication go through the context helpers (ctxSetToken and ctxSetReason, or however those build-specific helpers remain reachable), and the request-context setup (addNosurfContext/ctxClear) is invoked rather than bypassed by direct context API calls introduced into the portable files.
rubrics.rationale: The go1.7 versus !go1.7 split is implemented through those helpers; inlining context.WithValue-style access into shared code would silently break the legacy build configuration of this repository.

rubrics.criterion: No repaired function keeps an open-coded fragment of a recipe side by side with the helper that now owns it: the patch must remove the inline bodies it replaces, not add extraction helpers while leaving the local arithmetic in place (for example an unmask loop or a base64 decode call duplicated next to a call to the same capability).
rubrics.rationale: The instance's specific damage is coexisting copies; a patch that layers helpers onto the monoliths without deleting the inline fragments leaves the cleanup half-done even though calls were added.

rubrics.criterion: The flattening-era scaffolding is gone from the repaired code: none of the phase-banner comments introduced by the inlining (the dash-delimited section banners such as the intake, mint/bootstrap, admission routing, origin adjudication and credential comparison banners) or the pipe-simulation variables/comments that only described the inline layout remain in handler.go or token.go after the repair.
rubrics.rationale: Those banners and narrative comments were added by the flattening to fake structure inside the monoliths; retaining them after extraction keeps the misleading map alive and marks an unfinished repair.

rubrics.criterion: The repair does not strand the existing primitive implementations as parallel orphans: it must not leave freshly minted helpers implementing masking, encoding, comparison or minting while the pre-existing named primitives that already provide those capabilities (such as the masking, base64 and comparison functions the test suite imports directly) remain unreferenced by production code.
rubrics.rationale: The decomposed library already owns all the needed primitives; duplicating them under new names as part of the repair recreates the two-vocabularies problem this task exists to remove.

rubrics.criterion: The repair covers all flattened entry points: the patch must not re-decompose only the request pipeline (ServeHTTP) while leaving the token re-issuance method or the string-form verification function in their flattened form with their inline copies intact.
rubrics.rationale: A single-function fix is the most plausible incomplete repair for this instance, since the three owners can be refactored independently and each passes the suite on its own.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not change the security-relevant observable semantics: token equality is still decided by a constant-time comparison of raw 32-byte tokens, the raw form still goes to the cookie while the masked form still goes to the request container (Vary: Cookie still added), the one-time-pad masking scheme is untouched, the exemption/safe-method short-circuit still happens before origin checks, and the origin ladder still yields exactly ErrNoReferer, ErrBadReferer, ErrBadOrigin or ErrBadToken under the same inputs.
rubrics.rationale: These are the CSRF guarantees the middleware sells; regrouping code that silently drops constant-time comparison, mismatches the token forms or reorders the admission/origin/credential gates would be a correctness regression invisible to a structural review.

rubrics.criterion: The patch does not modify, weaken or delete test files, test fixtures or test helpers to make the refactor pass: the suite must pass against the refactor without the tests being adapted in any way.
rubrics.rationale: The suite imports the unexported primitives directly, so adapting the tests is the tempting shortcut that turns a behavior-preserving repair into a contract change.
